Overview:

12-Hour Offline AI Hack Day in Indore

About the Event:

Most hackathons end the exact same way: you spend the weekend writing code, show a slide deck, and after the event, the project is abandoned and forgotten.

We are here to change that.

Organised by TECHhelp4U and backed by Major League Hacking (MLH), with Google Gemini as the official technology partner, Stage 02 // System Matrix is an action-packed, 12-hour offline building sprint in Indore.

This isn't just a competition to win prizes—it’s a launchpad for your next venture. We want builders to step in with a founder mindset: pick a real problem, build a working AI product using code, and show a clear future roadmap for how you plan to turn your build into a real startup.

Top-performing teams will earn direct mentorship, ecosystem support, and fast-track invitations to Stage 03 (Kurukshetra) to help turn their prototypes into active companies!

Quick Highlights:

  • Venue: Indore, Madhya Pradesh (in-person offline venue)
  • Duration: 12-hour continuous offline sprint
  • Team Size: 2–4 members
  • Focus Area: 100% Artificial Intelligence (AI) powered by Google Gemini
  • Official Backing: Supported by Major League Hacking (MLH)
  • Perks: Exciting prizes for top podiums, plus assured swag kits, stickers, and goodies for every single participant!

What Should You Build? (100% AI Tracks):

Stage 02 is exclusively focused on artificial intelligence. We encourage teams to leverage Google Gemini to build intelligent, practical solutions across any of the following focus areas:

The Google Gemini Spotlight Track:

Build smart applications utilising Google Gemini's multimodal and large-context capabilities:

  • Multimodal Problem Solvers: Applications that process text, audio, images, and video together to solve real-world problems.
  • Deep Context Engines: Tools that analyse large repositories, documents, or knowledge bases in seconds.
  • Context-Aware Assistants: Helpful AI companions that understand user context and automate daily workflows.

Autonomous Agents & Workflows:

  • Self-operating task agents that can plan, execute, and troubleshoot without manual oversight.
  • Autonomous research, document synthesis, or customer support workflows.
  • Intelligent bots that assist software teams with code review, automated testing, or bug detection.

Developer & Creator Productivity Tools:

  • Smart developer tools, CLI utilities, and automated debugging assistants.
  • Workflow enhancers for writers, creators, designers, or product teams.

AI for Real-World Industry Impact:

  • Healthcare & Wellness: AI tools that help organise clinic notes, assist patients, or streamline records.
  • Education & Learning: Personalised interactive tutors and regional language learning tools.
  • Commerce & Small Businesses: Automated bookkeeping, smart support assistants, or intelligent fraud detection.

Competition Rounds & Structure:

Round 1: Online Application & Idea Screening (Online):

  • Register your team of 2–4 members on Unstop.
  • Submit a brief summary of the problem you want to solve, your planned AI architecture, and your team's background.
  • Shortlisted teams will receive official invitations and an entry badge for the offline finale in Indore.

Round 2: The 12-Hour Offline Hack Sprint (Indore):

  • Kickoff & Mentor Sync: Arrive at the venue, set up your workstation, and review your architecture with industry mentors.
  • Build Sprint: 12 hours of uninterrupted coding, debugging, and product development.
  • Live Demonstrations: Present your working project live to the jury and walk through your startup roadmap.
  • Awards & Goodies: Celebrate winning teams, collect your certificates and swag kits, and receive Stage 03 invitations!

Eligibility Criteria:

  • Open to all engineering, design, and management students from any college or university across India.
  • Working developers, early-stage founders, and independent builders are warmly welcome.
  • Cross-college and cross-specialisation teams are fully allowed and encouraged.
  • Team size must strictly be between 2 and 4 members.

What Do You Need to Submit?

Before the 12 hours run out, every team must submit three things:

  • GitHub Repository: A public repository showing active commits made during the event.
  • Live Product Demo: A working application running live. No video recordings or static Figma screens are allowed during judging.
  • Startup Roadmap (1-Page Summary or Short Slide Deck):
    • Target Customer: Who has this problem, and why will they use your solution?
    • Business Model: How will this product sustain itself or generate revenue?
    • Future Milestones: What are the next 3 to 6 steps you will take over the next 3 to 6 months to launch this?

How Will You Be Judged?

  • Working Prototype & Live Demo — 30%: Does the software actually function in real time? Is it responsive, usable, and stable?
  • AI Integration & Tech Depth — 30%: How effectively is AI, including Google Gemini, integrated into the core product logic? Is the code clean and well-structured?
  • Problem-Solution Fit & Startup Value — 20%: Does the project solve a real, painful problem that people or businesses would pay for?
  • Future Startup Roadmap — 20%: Does the team have a realistic 3-to-6-month post-hackathon plan to scale this into an active venture?

Perks, Rewards & What’s In It For You:

  • Exciting Prizes: Prestigious awards for top podium teams and track champions.
  • Assured Swag for Everyone: Exclusive event T-shirts, badge kits, stickers, and official MLH season badges for every single participant.
  • Food & Refreshments: Free meals, coffee, snacks, and energy drinks throughout the 12 hours.
  • Direct Mentorship: One-on-one architectural guidance from experienced AI engineers and founders.
  • Incubation Pathway: Fast-tracked selection into Stage 03 (Kurukshetra) with continuous guidance to help launch your startup.
  • Official Certificates: Verified certificates of participation and excellence backed by TECHhelp4U and partner networks.

Code of Conduct & Guidelines:

  • All participants must adhere strictly to the MLH Code of Conduct.
  • Plagiarism, pre-built applications, or submitting projects built before the hackathon start time will lead to immediate disqualification.
  • Respect your peers, mentors, and venue staff at all times.

Let's stop building disposable hackathon demos and start building real AI startups!
